article.title: Genocide Charges Against Israeli Leaders
article.author: Marjorie Cohn
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. A s Israelis went to the polls last Tuesday to decide who will next preside over Israel’s continuing genocide, a U.N. Commission issued a devastating report on the day before the election. It documents how Israel is importing its Gaza strategy of total destruction into the West Bank. And as the Trump administration escalates its efforts to disable the International Criminal Court with punishing sanctions to prevent prosecution of Israeli leaders for their crimes, the Commission’s report recommends that the ICC seriously consider charging Israeli leaders with genocide in addition to war crimes and crimes against humanity. In November 2024, the ICC issued arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Defense Minister Yoav Gallant for war crimes and crimes against humanity stemming from their actions in Gaza since October 7, 2023. This was the first time the ICC issued arrest warrants against any Israeli official for crimes against the Palestinian people. Netanyahu and Gallant stand charged with the war crimes of starvation as a form of warfare, and intentional attacks on civilians; as well as the crimes against humanity of murder, persecution, and other inhumane acts. Despite the ruling 10 months earlier by the International Court of Justice on Jan. 26, 2024 that Israel was plausibly committing genocide, former ICC Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan did not seek arrest warrants for Netanyahu and Gallant for the crime of genocide. Related: Trump's Attack on the ICC Exposes America's Double Standard on War Crimes Raji Sourani, director of Palestinian Centre for Human Rights, who praised Khan’s May 2024 applications for the arrest warrants, urged the ICC prosecutor to also secure “warrants for the crime of genocide given the staggering evidence of genocidal acts and intent made by top Israeli officials.” Likewise, international law expert Richard Falk, while calling Khan’s requests for warrants against Netanyahu and Gallant “historic,” said the crime of genocide was “the elephant in the room.” He wrote, “Over time I suspect that the failure to address ‘genocide’ will be regarded as the most shocking weakness in the prosecutor’s formal statement.” Now a U.N. Commission is seeking to rectify that weakness. Commission Finds Israel Continues to Commit Genocide Former U.S. Secretary of Defense Lloyd Austin, left, with Netanyahu and Gallant in Tel Aviv, Oct. 13, 2023. (DoD, Chad J. McNeeley, CC BY 2.0) The U.N. Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and Israel (“the Commission”) transmitted its new report to the General Assembly on Oct. 26. It documented Israeli war crimes, and the crimes against humanity of extermination, persecution, torture, rape and other forms of sexual violence as part of a larger attack aimed at subjugating and displacing the Palestinian people. “The intentional killing and injuring of Palestinian civilians and destruction of homes in the West Bank combined with Israel’s persistent denial of responsibility form part of a broader strategy to exterminate and displace Palestinians and impose conditions of life that are unliveable,” Srinivasan Muralidhar, chair of the Commission, said in a statement. “Meanwhile, Israel’s expansion of territorial control in Gaza continues to result in the killing and harming of Palestinian civilians who approach or cross the Yellow Line,” he said. The Commission concluded that “Israeli authorities and forces continue to commit genocidal acts with the genocidal intent to destroy, in whole or in part, the Palestinians in Gaza.” Genocide is defined by the 1948 Genocide Convention as acts committed “with intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnical, racial, or religious group,” including killing members of the group, inflicting serious bodily or mental harm on members of the group, or deliberately inflicting conditions of life calculated to bring about the group’s physical destruction in whole or in part. Related: The 2026 Midterms May Not End on Election Day 1,400+ Civilians Killed in ‘Ceasefire’ The Commission referenced its earlier 2025 report, which documented Israel’s genocidal act including “deliberately carry[ing] out acts inflicting death and severe bodily and mental harm on Palestinian children,” and “systematically destroying Palestinian life.” It cited the “specific intent of the Israeli authorities to commit genocide against the Palestinian group in Gaza.” Since Oct. 7, 2023, Israeli forces have killed more than 75,000 Palestinians across the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including at least 21,500 children, and 11,000 women. A “so-called ceasefire” (in the Commission’s words) was declared on Oct. 10, 2025. But since then, Israeli forces have killed over 1,431 people, including at least 300 children, and wounded 5,026, as of September 30, 2026. Between January 2025 and August 2026, Israeli military actions drove more than 34,000 Palestinians from their homes. The Commission called it the largest displacement of Palestinians in the West Bank since 1967, when Israel captured the territory from Jordan. In its new report, the Commission noted a “strategic shift” in Israeli military operations in the West Bank since January 2025, including “widespread destruction of Palestinian housing and infrastructure.” Operation Iron Wall “reflects the import of the Gaza strategy of total destruction into West Bank operations.” IDF soldiers raiding Jenin, Occupied West Bank, January 2025, (IDF Spokesperson’s Unit/Wikimedia Commons/ CC BY-SA 3.0) The Commission documented several instances of sexual violence against Palestinians by Israeli authorities in Gaza. They included multiple insertions of a metal detector into the anus of one victim; tying a plastic cord around the genitals of another victim during interrogation for a long period of time; and the rape of a victim with a stick, then forcing him to insert it into his mouth until he vomited. Israel’s acts of sexual violence, the Commission wrote, “continue to be a part of the pattern to destroy the Palestinians as a group in Gaza.” The Commission also documented examples of sexual violence in the West Bank. One victim was gang raped several times with objects while prison guards mocked and photographed him, squeezed his penis, and threatened they would cut it off until he screamed in pain. And the report noted two cases of sexual violence, including rape, against participants in the 2025 Global Sumud Flotilla. The Commission’s Recommendations The Commission recommended that the ICC prosecutor “examine, within its continuing investigation in the Situation in the State of Palestine, the crimes committed in Gaza and the West Bank, including genocide, crimes against humanity, and war crimes for amendment to existing arrest warrants and addition to future application for arrest warrants.” In addition, the Commission recommended that Israel immediately end the commission of genocide in Gaza, and fulfill its obligations to prevent and punish genocide and incitement to genocide under the Genocide Convention. It also recommended that Israel comply with the July 2024 advisory opinion of the International Court of Justice, immediately end its unlawful occupation of Palestinian territory, stop all new settlement activities, remove all settlers and settlements, and remove all obstacles to the full exercise of the Palestinian people’s right to self-determination. The Commission recommended that Israel fully comply with international human rights law and international humanitarian law in military and law enforcement operations, and stop targeting civilians and civilian objects indispensable to the survival of a people. And it recommended that Israel prosecute and punish all who commit violations of international humanitarian and human rights law. In a statement, the Council on American-Islamic Relations said : “Once again, the United Nations has concluded what has been obvious to all those who have observed Israel’s actions in Gaza and the West Bank. Slaughtering tens of thousands of people, starving an entire civilian population, detaining them in facilities in which they are tortured, expelling tens of thousands more from their homes – these are crimes against humanity and genocide. The murderous Israeli government must be held accountable for its atrocities.” Consortiuum News
